properties.name: A state the design deliberately chose is not reported as a defect, so doing the right thing stops degrading the instrument
properties.statement:
When a design has RULED that a node is correctly attached to nothing, or correctly unsatisfied, a detector must be able to see that ruling and report the node accordingly — rather than counting a deliberate state as a structural defect. (Distinct from the FACT the guard named, which records one measured instance; this is the intent that answers it and a second instance besides.)

⭐ THE SHAPE THAT MAKES THIS URGENT, in the reporter's words: THE DISPOSITION RULE AND THE DEFECT DETECTOR MAKE EACH OTHER UNREADABLE, AND THE DIRECTION IS THE BAD ONE — THE CORRECT ACTION DEGRADES THE INSTRUMENT. It is self-reinforcing: a later seat watching the count climb has an incentive to stop registering documents and leave them absent, which is the worse state.

TWO MEASURED INSTANCES:

(a) `orphan_node` FIRES ON THE STATE A STANDING RULING PRESCRIBES. A fleet has a ruling for dated per-increment scope proposals whose increment has shipped: register the Artifact, record WHY no claims were extracted, draw NO claim edges. A `DOCUMENTS` edge would be false — it would count a superseded document as coverage in their ingest ledger, which buckets on exactly that edge — and absence would be false too, a pretend backlog someone re-mines. "Registered, no doctrine, on purpose" is the correct end state. Measured: defects moved 88 → 97 across ten artifact writes, eight of them deliberate no-claim registrations, with 31 more documents owed in the same genre. A boss reading "97 structural defects" cannot tell the deliberate ones from the real ones.
   ⭐ AND THE TOOL ALREADY CONTAINS THE SENTENCE THAT EXONERATES THE NODE: its own `repair_is_a_judgement` text reads "a parked thought that correctly governs nothing yet" — accurate, and it files the node as a problem anyway.

(b) `disconnected_community` CANNOT SEE AN INTENDED-UNSATISFIED RULING. A requirement was disconnected on purpose, recorded in an accepted Decision saying no SATISFIES may be drawn to it. The detector's suggested fix is `generate_bridge` — PRECISELY THE FORGERY THE RULING FORBIDS — and an agent working the defect list top-down would do it.

WHAT IS OWED, cheapest first as they filed it: a first-class marker for "attached to nothing ON PURPOSE" — their COORD.md already calls this PARKED in prose and the schema has no word for it — with `orphan_node` skipping it and reporting `parked: N` separately; and a way for a Decision that governs a requirement's unsatisfied-ness to be visible to the structural detector, so it can say "unsatisfied BY RULING (see dec:…)".

WHY NOT JUST ACKNOWLEDGE: `acknowledge_defect` exists and stores a reason, but acknowledging 31 findings one at a time to record ONE ruling is the wrong shape, and the acknowledgement expires "when the shape changes" on nodes whose shape is deliberately fixed.

RELATED AND SETTLED THE OTHER WAY, named so this does not reopen it: `dec:report-dont-judge` says reflow2 reports and never ranks. This is not a request to judge — it is a request to READ A RULING THE DESIGN ALREADY MADE, the same move `designation: required` made for `unprovided_interface` on 2026-08-09.

⚠️ BOUND THE REPORTER STATED AND I HAVE NOT CLOSED: they did not check whether the guard built for the `DOCUMENTS`/`REALIZES` asymmetry was meant to cover this case and misses it, or whether this case was never contemplated. Those are different reports and only the second is evidenced.

REPORTED BY dev_storyflow's fleet, 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-15.
